executedInR1: The independent oracle (O1) on the 13 registered oracleControls in templates.json. These compile and run registrant-written C# only; no Calor compiler code runs.

Lex-and-parse validity of every generated case, and compilation with VerifyContracts=false and VerifyRefinements=false of every case outside the IMPL-*, SIMP-*, and CTRL-RETRO-845 rows (those are parse-only, because full compilation would run the always-on inheritance checker (Z3) or the simplifier under test), on the working tree whose src/ tree equals B1's. baselines.role: retrospective pre-fix control baseline (control rows only; never a sweep baseline)

binary.procedure: As B1, at this commit. Runs only the CTRL-RETRO-845 cases, preceded by the CTRL-POSITIVE and CTRL-NEGATIVE solver-availability check (charged to the reserve).

noPooling.rule: B1 and N1 are separate sweeps over the same frozen case list. Every result row carries exactly one baseline id. No count, rate, row status, disposition, or finding is computed over the union, and a result on one baseline never substitutes for a missing, invalid, timed-out, or not-investigated result on the other.
noPooling.crossBaselineUse: A finding on one baseline is re-run on the other baseline from the minimization reserve and recorded as that baseline's own result (reproduces / does-not-reproduce / not-run). The other baseline's row status uses only its own results.

denominator.derivation: Rows are derived from the verifier source at B1 (equal to N1 for src/Calor.Compiler/Verification): ModeledForms in ContractTranslator.cs (scalar types, array element types, expression kinds, binary/unary operators, string operations, comparison modes, quantifier bound-variable types), the assumption demotions and refusals in Z3Verifier.cs and FunctionBodyEncoder, the obligation kinds in ObligationTracker.cs (solver not whitelist-gated), the implication prover used by ContractInheritanceChecker and calor verify --weakening-check, the verification cache, the contract simplification pass that runs before both verification and emission, and the elision sites in CSharpEmitter.cs.
frozenWhitelist: scalar-types: i8, i16, i32, i64, u8, u16, u32, u64, bool, str
array-element-types: i8, i16, i32, i64, u8, u16, u32, u64 (with synthetic $length)

expression-kinds: IntLiteralNode, BoolLiteralNode, StringLiteralNode, ReferenceNode, BinaryOperationNode, UnaryOperationNode, ConditionalExpressionNode, ForallExpressionNode, ExistsExpressionNode, ImplicationExpressionNode, ArrayAccessNode, ArrayLengthNode, FieldAccessNode, StringOperationNode, SelfRefNode
binary-operators: Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Modulo, Equal, NotEqual, LessThan, LessOrEqual, GreaterThan, GreaterOrEqual, And, Or, BitwiseAnd, BitwiseOr, BitwiseXor, LeftShift, RightShift
string-operations: Length, Contains, StartsWith, EndsWith, Equals, IsNullOrEmpty, IndexOf, Substring, SubstringFrom, Concat

string-comparison-modes: Ordinal only — a non-ordinal mode is refused, and StartsWith/EndsWith/IndexOf require ':ordinal' EXPLICITLY (.NET resolves their no-mode overloads to CurrentCulture; Contains/Equals are ordinal)
quantifier-bound-variable-types: any declarable type except floating-point (unmodeled types become uninterpreted sorts)
denominator.frozenWhitelistSource: ModeledForms.RenderWhitelist() at B1, byte-equal to the generated appendix of docs/verification-modeled-forms.md at B1 (file SHA-256 c296720f268c497cf93e3d27943f3a0a750ed09abce3badcb5822c4e0bd5e932, the hash DifferentialGate pins).
denominator.whitelistCoverage: Every whitelist member maps to at least one row with cases (enforced by SoundnessRegistrationTests). Members outside the whitelist that the code can still reach are registered as refusal rows (Power and other operators, BitwiseNot outside the obligation solver, floating point, calls, Replace and other string operations, non-ordinal modes).

classifications.modeled: Proven (non-vacuous) or Discharged may be produced and may remove a guard; the oracle decides whether it is true.
classifications.assumed: The form must not produce an unconditional Proven/Discharged; Assumed is the strongest legitimate outcome (string-model, reference-model, checked-arithmetic, exceptional-path or contract-division assumptions).
classifications.unsupported-refused: The form must produce Unsupported or be rejected by the compiler before verification.
classifications.not-investigated: Excluded before execution with a recorded reason; never release-critical; zero cases.

simplpass.symbols: ContractSimplificationPass.Simplify (runs before verification AND before emission)

channels.CH-CONTRACT: Program.Compile(source, "case.calr", CompilationOptions { VerifyContracts = true, VerifyRefinements = false, EnableTypeChecking = TypeCheckingDefault, ContractMode = Debug, VerificationTimeoutMs = 5000, VerificationCacheOptions = { Enabled = false } }) run twice: ElideProvenGuards = true (the default user path) and ElideProvenGuards = false. Outcomes are read from options.VerificationResults (ContractVerificationResult.EffectiveOutcome: Status, IsVacuous, Assumptions).
channels.CH-OBLIGATION: As CH-CONTRACT with VerifyRefinements = true; outcomes are read from options.ObligationResults (Obligation.Outcome, Status, Kind). This is the path behind calor_refine (MCP) and the public API; the CLI and MSBuild task do not solve obligations at B1/N1.
channels.CH-IMPLICATION: The inheritance checker that Program.Compile always runs (Z3 when available). Each IMPL template carries contracts in exactly one direction (interface/implementer §Q, or §S), so at most one implication is checked per case; its outcome is read from the Calor0815 info diagnostic text ('Precondition weakening proven' or the postcondition counterpart: Proven) and the LSP-violation error diagnostics (Failed), attributed to the implementing method. Any other Calor0815 on the case is archived, not adjudicated. A case with no implication diagnostic is no-claim.
channels.CH-CACHE: CH-CONTRACT with VerificationCacheOptions { Enabled = true, ProjectDirectory = <fresh per-case temp dir> }: compile calorPrime, then calor, in the same directory; then a cold compile of calor in a new directory. CACHE-SEMANTICS-VERSION rewrites every primed entry's translator semantics version string to 'r1-stale-version' between the two compiles.
channels.CH-CLI-CROSSCHECK: For CTRL-* cases only: the baseline CLI (calor --input case.calr --output case.g.cs --verify --verbose --format json --no-telemetry) must not contradict the in-process channel on any contract it reports (the CLI omits some Proven diagnostics, so absence is not a contradiction). A contradiction makes the run invalid (harness defect), not a finding.
channels.invocation: In-process only: the baseline's calor.dll is loaded into a collectible AssemblyLoadContext with its own Microsoft.Z3.dll and native libz3, and Calor.Compiler.Program.Compile and CompilationOptions are bound by reflection by name. There is no fallback channel (the CLI envelope does not carry every outcome and both emissions). If a baseline cannot be loaded in-process, that baseline's run is invalid; after the invalid-run limit its release-critical rows are BLOCKED.

perCase: Compile the case once per channel listed for its row; record raw statuses, IsVacuous, assumption lists, counterexample models, diagnostics, and both emitted C# texts.

Map each claim-bearing raw status to exactly one contract §4 token: Proven, ProvenVacuous, Discharged, Assumed, Unsupported, TimeoutOrUnavailable, Failed, Boundary. Map from ProofOutcome (Status, IsVacuous, Assumptions), never from a legacy enum. An unmapped status is a harness error (contract E001), never the nearest token.

A case the baseline compiler rejects with an error diagnostic before verification is recorded as compile-rejected (no token), with its error codes. It validates a refusal only on an unsupported-refused row and only if every error code is in that row's frontEndRefusalCodes (frozen at B1; an empty list means the form must reach the verifier and be Unsupported). Any other rejection is harness-invalid for that baseline, including on N1 if its different front end rejects with other codes.

Guard observation: in the elision-enabled emission the claim's guard must be absent iff the token is Proven (postcondition, non-vacuous) or Discharged with an ObligationPolicy action needing no guard; in the forced emission it must be present.
observation.claimSite: Exactly one claim per case, fixed by the template's claimSite. Other contracts in the same case are archived but not adjudicated.
observation.translatorSemanticsVersion: Recorded per run from the loaded assembly's ContractTranslator.SemanticsVersion (z3-executable-semantics-v2 at B1 and N1).

oracle.definition: For each case, the registrant-authored C# in templates.json (rendered per case by SweepCaseGenerator) is compiled with Roslyn against BCL assemblies only and executed over the case's registered input domain, under CultureInfo en-US and the module's overflow mode (checked unless the template says unchecked). It never references or loads a Calor assembly and never calls the verifier's translator, simplifier, emitter, solver, or cache. Implementation: tests/Calor.Compiler.Tests/SoundnessRegistration/IndependentOracle.cs.
semantics: forall claims (postcondition, obligation, implication): for every input with Hyp true and a normally-returning Body, Prop must evaluate to true without throwing. Inputs where Hyp is false are excluded; inputs where Hyp or Body throws are excluded and counted (normal-return semantics, D5). A Prop that is false or throws is a violation.

exists claims (precondition satisfiability): a witness is an input where Prop is true. Adjudication: Proven with a solver model that satisfies Prop under O1 -> validated-proof; Proven when O1 is no-witness-exhaustive -> false-unconditional-proof; Proven with a model that does not satisfy Prop -> spurious-model (a finding; the claim may still be true); Proven, no usable model, and no-witness-sampled -> unconfirmed-claim (blocks CLEAN); Failed (unsatisfiable) with an O1 witness -> spurious-refutation. The non-vacuity check for an exists claim is the satisfying witness itself.

Exhaustive when every domain parameter is bool or an 8/16-bit integer without an override list and the product is at most 65,536 inputs; otherwise the domain is the per-type boundary table plus 6 seeded values per parameter plus every numeric constant drawn into the case with its neighbours (v-1, v, v+1, within the parameter's type), capped at 4,096 tuples by seeded subsampling. A sampled domain can show violation but never establishes truth.

Where C# defines no semantics (u64 mixed with a signed operand; unary minus on ulong in H1), the oracle uses exact mathematical integers (System.Numerics.BigInteger) and the row is a refusal or hypothesis row.
oracle.evaluationBudget: 60 s wall clock per case; exceeding it is oracle-invalid.

corroboration.definition: The baseline's emitted C# with forced guards (ElideProvenGuards = false) is compiled with the baseline's Calor.Runtime.dll and executed (via the template's replay expression, or Probe(args) by position) on every O1 witness and on the first 16 reached inputs in domain order (IndependentOracle.ReplaySampleSize; this includes D15's i == 3 input). O2 records whether the forced guard throws ContractViolationException / InvalidOperationException.
corroboration.role: Corroboration and divergence detection only. O2 runs post-simplification code (ContractSimplificationPass rewrites contracts before emission), so it shares the simplifier's assumptions and can never be the sole oracle.

oracle.divergence: If O1 says the property is violated on a replayed input and the forced O2 guard does not throw, or O1 says it holds on a replayed reached input and the forced guard throws, the case additionally gets a semantic-divergence record for #1413. The O1 verdict is not changed by O2.
oracle.partialEnumeration: A violation (or, for exists, a witness) found before the 60 s budget runs out is conclusive and kept; only an inconclusive partial enumeration is oracle-invalid.

generation.method: Deterministic template expansion. templates.json holds every template; each template has a row, an instance count, holes, Calor text, and oracle text. Case ids are R1-<row>-<nnn> numbered within the row in template order. Each case uses SplitMix64 seeded with masterSeed XOR the first 8 bytes (little-endian) of SHA-256(caseId).
generation.coverageHoles: Holes of kind cycle/cyclePairs take option (instance mod n), so every advertised member is rendered (minInstances guarantees n instances). Whitelist coverage is checked against the generated case texts, not template options.
generation.caseIndexRule: cases-index.json lists every case id with its row, template, claim, exhaustive flag, and the SHA-256 of its Calor text, prime text, and oracle text. A test regenerates the cases and fails on any byte difference, so the case set cannot change without a visible edit to a hashed file.

budget.unit: One case execution = one case run on one baseline through all of its row's channels (including both emissions and O2 replay). The 1,500 ceiling counts case executions across B1, N1, and P845 combined; the existing 1,170-cell verifier-runtime differential and existing regression tests are not counted and are not re-run by #1311.
budget.reserveUse: Only for (a) minimizing a candidate finding, (b) re-running a finding's case on the other baseline, (c) the single permitted retry of an inconclusive attempt. Reserve executions are labeled and never raise a row to clean.
budget.retryCost: A retry is a case execution and is charged to the reserve.

execution.order: Round-robin by case index across rows (case 1 of every row, then case 2, ...), in row order of this file; B1 and N1 alternate per case; controls run first on each baseline. A timebox stop therefore leaves coverage spread across rows instead of chosen.
execution.retry: A case whose claim token is TimeoutOrUnavailable, or whose execution crashed or exceeded caseWallClockSeconds, is retried exactly once with identical inputs. Both attempts are retained. If the attempts disagree the case status is flaky (never established). If any attempt is Proven or Discharged with an O1 violation, that is a finding regardless of the other attempt. There is no third attempt.

environment.dotnetSdk: global.json at each baseline pins 10.0.100 with rollForward latestMinor; the exact `dotnet --version` is recorded in pins.json and must not change within a baseline's sweep (the registrant's machine reported 10.0.401).
environment.os: Recorded (uname -a or Windows build) in pins.json; one OS/architecture per baseline sweep.
environment.culture: CultureInfo.CurrentCulture = en-US for O1 and O2 execution; restored afterwards.
environment.z3Seed: No seed is injected into the baseline compiler; production behavior is what is under test. Nondeterminism is handled by the retry rule (determinism itself is #1421/#1135, out of scope).
environment.parallelism: Cases run sequentially within a baseline process.

invalidRunPolicy: A run is invalid if: a pinned binary or native hash differs; dotnet --version changes mid-sweep; any oracleControl does not produce its registered verdict on the executing machine; CH-CLI-CROSSCHECK disagrees; or more than 10% of a baseline's cases crash in the harness (not in the compiler).

Invalid runs are archived under attempts/ with the reason and are never used for row status, except that any Proven/Discharged attempt with an O1 violation recorded in an invalid run becomes a candidate-unconfirmed finding and its case is re-executed first in the next valid run; it is not discarded.

After an invalid run the harness may be fixed and the baseline restarted from its first case with the same case list. At most 3 invalid runs per baseline; a fourth makes every unexecuted release-critical row of that baseline BLOCKED.
A compiler crash or compile rejection on a case is a case result, not a harness crash.

Solver availability: on every baseline (including P845) the CTRL-POSITIVE and CTRL-NEGATIVE cases must all produce their expectedOutcome before any other case. Any mismatch (for example a missing solver turning proofs into TimeoutOrUnavailable) invalidates the run; it is never read as a completeness result.

classes.false-unconditional-proof: Claim token Proven (non-vacuous) or Discharged with a passed non-vacuity check, and O1 verdict violated. The contract's release-blocking finding.
classes.false-proof-unconfirmed-vacuity: Discharged, O1 violated, but the non-vacuity check did not pass. Still a finding for #1413.
classes.required-demotion-absent: Proven/Discharged on an assumed or unsupported-refused row without an O1 violation in the domain.
classes.guard-elided-without-proof: The claim's guard is absent in the elision-enabled emission while the token is not Proven/Discharged, or is absent in the forced emission.
classes.vacuity-mislabel: Proven reported non-vacuous while O1 is exhaustive and vacuous-in-domain, or ProvenVacuous while O1 found a reached input.
classes.spurious-refutation: Failed whose replayed counterexample (or, for exhaustive domains, any input) does not violate the property under O1. A completeness defect; needs a disposition.
classes.stale-cache-proof: A warm (cached) compile yields a different claim token from the cold compile of the same text (for CACHE-SEMANTICS-VERSION variant B: any token other than the cold one).
classes.semantic-divergence: O1 and O2 disagree on an input (see oracle.divergence).
classes.candidate-unconfirmed: A finding whose minimization or standalone C# reproduction did not complete inside capacity. Stays a finding.
classes.validated-proof: Proven/Discharged (non-vacuous, non-vacuity check passed for Discharged) on a modeled row, O1 holds-exhaustive or holds-sampled with at least one reached input. Sampled means no counterexample was found within the domain, not that the property holds.
classes.refusal-validated: Assumed, Unsupported, or compile-rejected where the row requires that, with guards retained.
classes.no-claim: Assumed, Unsupported, TimeoutOrUnavailable, Failed (with a genuine counterexample), or Boundary on a modeled row. Establishes nothing.
classes.harness-invalid: The case could not be evaluated on this baseline (oracle-invalid, compile-rejected on a modeled or assumed row, a front-end rejection on a refused row whose error codes are not all in that row's frontEndRefusalCodes, unmappable status). Counted and reported; never replaced by another case.
classes.unconfirmed-claim: Proven on an exists claim with no usable model and no O1 witness in a sampled domain.
classes.spurious-model: Proven on an exists claim whose solver model does not satisfy the property under O1.
classes.control-mismatch: A verifier control (other than the solver-availability check) whose token differs from its expectedOutcome on B1 or N1. A finding for #1413; a Proven with an O1 violation is a false-unconditional-proof instead.
classes.flaky: Two attempts disagree (contract non-outcome status). Never established.

caseResults.nonVacuityCheck: For every Discharged (and every Proven) claim, O1 must report at least one reached input (Hyp true, Body returned normally). Recorded as nonVacuityCheck {id: "R1-O1-reached", result: "passed" | "failed"}. Required by contract §4 condition 5 for Discharged.
rowStatus: FALSE-PROOF if any case is false-unconditional-proof.
else FINDING if any case is any other finding class.

else INCOMPLETE if any allocated case is unexecuted, harness-invalid, flaky, crashed, unconfirmed-claim, or still TimeoutOrUnavailable after its retry. There is no tolerance: one such case blocks CLEAN.

else CLEAN-WITHIN-BUDGET, reported with the counts of validated-proof, refusal-validated, and no-claim cases and the share of exhaustive domains. A modeled row with zero validated-proof cases is reported as CLEAN-WITHIN-BUDGET (no establishing outcome observed): it supports no release claim that relies on a Proven/Discharged result for that form.
caseResults.rowStatusToContract: CLEAN-WITHIN-BUDGET is the only status #1413 may disposition VALIDATED, and it means no counterexample was found within this matrix and budget. INCOMPLETE release-critical rows are BLOCKED at the timebox (contract §8 stopping condition 2). Row status is per baseline.

fields.registrationCommit: full SHA of the merge that froze this registration

witness.o2: guard threw | did not throw | not-run

minimized.csharpReproduction: standalone C# that shows the property false without Calor

fields.attempts: every attempt with timestamps and raw output paths
fields.affectedGuarantee: the modeled form, the guard-elision path, and any public claim or experiment that relies on it
fields.disposition: null until #1413 records exactly one of the frozen findingDispositions

rules: Every registered row on each baseline and every finding gets exactly one disposition from #1413, recorded per baseline.
VALIDATED only for CLEAN-WITHIN-BUDGET rows; never for a row with a finding.
NOT-INVESTIGATED only for the not-investigated rows of this registration (XCL-*). An unexecuted registered row is not eligible: it is BLOCKED or MILESTONE-FAILED.

A false-unconditional-proof needs FIX-IN-0.24 or DEMOTE-IN-0.24 within the contract's s2-repairs (6 PRs) and s2-repair-size (600 lines) ceilings, or MILESTONE-FAILED. A retained guard does not cure it.

A fix or demotion lands on the post-repair candidate (#1423); the N1 package and the B1 tag are immutable, so their findings stay recorded as findings against those releases with the candidate-side disposition.

controls.oracleControls: templates.json oracleControls: 13 registrant C# properties with known verdicts (positive: holds; negative: violated with a registered witness; exists and vacuity cases). Executed in R1 by SoundnessRegistrationTests and re-executed by #1311 on its machine before any case (invalid-run policy).
controls.verifierControls: CTRL-POSITIVE, CTRL-NEGATIVE, CTRL-MUTATION, CTRL-RETRO-845, and CTRL-RETRO-FIXED cases carry an exact expectedOutcome. #1311 runs them first on each baseline. CTRL-POSITIVE/CTRL-NEGATIVE mismatches invalidate the run (solver availability). Any other mismatch on B1 or N1 is a control-mismatch finding; a Proven with an O1 violation is a false-unconditional-proof finding. A retrospective vector whose observation differs from expectedOutcome on B1 or N1 means a fixed defect may have regressed: it is a finding that #1413 must disposition, and the rows listed in the template's guards field cannot be dispositioned VALIDATED before it is.
controls.mutationControls: CTRL-MUTATION pairs M1 (behavior-preserving rewrite) and M2 (contract-preserving rewrite). The oracle verdicts within a pair must be equal; the verifier tokens may differ, and a differing token alone is not a finding (changed behavior is not a false proof).

retrospective845.cases: CTRL-RETRO-845 (6 cases, each with expectedOutcome for B1/N1 and p845ExpectedOutcome). Two are the shape named in #845 (ULONG bounds near ulong.MaxValue; pre-#961 the translator refused unsigned literals above int.MaxValue, so P845 is expected Unsupported: these two document the named shape and do not discriminate). Four discriminate the defect #961 actually fixed: in-range LONG:/UINT: literals were translated as signed 32-bit, so under overflow=unchecked x + LONG:1 and x + UINT:1 wrapped at int.MaxValue in the solver while C# widens to long.
retrospective845.discrimination: The control discriminates only if, for at least one of the four width cases, P845 produces exactly its p845ExpectedOutcome (Proven on a violated case, or Failed on a satisfiable case) while B1 (and, separately, N1) produces exactly its expectedOutcome. P845 must first pass the solver-availability check. If no width case discriminates, the control is reported as non-discriminating, not as a pass.
retrospective845.residual: #845 stays open; its named regression is not identified as a closing test (contract §11).

controls.existingDifferential: bench/phase0-agent-native/verifier-runtime-differential.json (65 forms, 1,170 cells) is cited as an existing control on the cutoff tree. It runs in CI on the current tree, not on the B1/N1 binaries, and is not part of this sweep's denominator or budget.

hypotheses.statement: ExpressionSimplifier folds unary Negate and BitwiseNot over IntLiteralNode without regard to IsUnsigned or IsLong, which could reach an established proof.
hypotheses.readingAtRegistration: Source reading at B1 (not execution): ExpressionSimplifier.Visit(UnaryOperationNode) returns early unless the operand is an IntLiteralNode with IsLong=false and IsUnsigned=false, so the unsigned/long case appears gated; BitwiseNot is folded although it is not in ModeledForms.UnaryOperators, so a folded literal can enter the whitelisted surface. Both readings are hypotheses; neither was tested.
hypotheses.cases: The SIMP-H1-UNARY-FOLD row (casesPerBaseline in denominator.rows); exact-integer oracle, except that negating int.MinValue throws under checked C#.

s1: Stop at the first of: 10 calendar days after this registration's merge; 20 agent-hours; 1,500 case executions; 600 CI runner-minutes; 10 local machine-hours. Record which ceiling stopped the sweep.

At a stop, unreached cases are not-investigated; every release-critical row with an unreached case is INCOMPLETE and therefore BLOCKED unless a reviewed #1407 amendment raising the ceiling merges first.
A finding does not stop the sweep. It is minimized from the reserve, filed, and the sweep continues in registered order.

No row, template, case, classification, oracle rule, or result class changes after the freeze except by a versioned amendment to this registration (version, UTC timestamp, justification, reviewed PR, afterDecisionBearingInspection flag). An amendment cannot remove a row or case; removed items stay reported with their last status. Cases added after the freeze are labeled post-registration: they can add findings but never contribute to CLEAN-WITHIN-BUDGET.

owners.implementation: Claude Code agent under #1311 (one branch, at most 2 PRs per the agent-prs-per-gate ceiling); agents never merge.
owners.templateAuthorship: The #1311 executor does not edit templates.json, the generator, or the oracle; a defect in them is fixed only by amendment.
